subject: SSQ: Data segmentation & export routing - clarification
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@quantumhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: SSQ: Data segmentation and export routing clarification

Karthik/Laura,

Thanks for taking a look at our security questionnaire. A few items came up in the privacy section where we need clarification before we sign the annex:

1) Data segmentation: can you confirm whether customer PII is logically tenant-isolated (per-tenant KV namespaces) in Redwood Dedicated, or is isolation implemented via access controls on shared storage? We need to be explicit for our DPA.

2) Export routing: our legal team wants to understand if log exports (audit logs, request traces) ever contain partially reconstructed PII (email, username) and whether those exports can be restricted to a single region or pushed to our S3 in us-east-1.

3) Dataflow diagram: would you be able to share a diagram that shows request ingress, KV cache, model hosting, and where pseudonymization/tokenization occurs? A visual helps the SSQ reviewers.

I've attached the SSQ spreadsheet with our highlighted rows (ssq_questions.xlsx). Can you also point us to the person on your side who owns artifact delivery (SOC2 evidence / diagrams)?

Cheers,
Daniel
Security & Privacy Lead
QuantumHealth

Attachments: ssq_questions.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@quantumhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: SSQ: Data segmentation and export routing clarification

Hi Daniel —

Appreciate the detailed notes. Quick answers up front, with a simple diagram attached (initial_dataflow_v1.png) for the reviewers. I'll have Marcus and Laura add detail on logging and artifact handoff.

1) Segmentation: For Redwood Dedicated we provide logical tenant isolation via per-tenant namespaces for persistent artifacts (KV namespaces + dedicated model routing). Runtime memory (KV cache) is scoped per-request/tenant at the serving layer; we do not store per-request PII in persistent logs by default. For customers needing FIPS/KMS separation we also offer a Private deployment where keys live in your KMS.

2) Export routing: Audit logs and request traces can include identifiers at the request-level when customers opt-in for debug exports. By default, we redact high-risk PII (full email, SSNs) from logs and only include hashed identifiers. Exports can be configured to route to a customer-controlled S3 bucket in a single region (e.g., us-east-1). We can add an export filter to strip additional fields prior to export.

3) Dataflow diagram: attached PNG shows ingress -> auth -> request router -> serving pool -> KV cache -> response. Pseudonymization/tokenization can be applied at two points: client-side (recommended) and server-side at the router stage before persistent storage.

Next steps: Marcus will confirm default retention windows for traces and Laura will provide the SOC2 and evidence delivery owner. If you want, we can set a 30-min sync to walk the diagram and confirm the export filters.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: initial_dataflow_v1.png

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@quantumhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: SSQ: Data segmentation and export routing clarification

Hi Daniel —

Following up with the specifics you asked for so your SSQ reviewers can map controls to evidence. Quick bullets:

- Access controls: role-based access (RBAC) enforced at both control plane and host level. Minimum-privilege roles: Viewer (read-only), Operator (deployment/metrics), Security (log access), Customer Admin (customer-managed keys).
- Log handling: application logs are sanitized by default using our redaction pipeline. Traces may contain request identifiers; PII fields (email, phone, SSN) are redacted or hashed before storage unless a customer explicitly toggles debug export.
- Retention: default audit log retention is 90 days for Hosted; Dedicated offers configurable retention down to 30 days or on-prem retention on Private.
- Export filters: we support field-level export policies. Example policy names: export_strip_pii_v1, export_hash_userids.
- Evidence handoff: SOC 2 report and control mappings are owned by our Trust team (trust@redwood.com). Marcus will send you a secure DocuSign/portal link for artifact access.

I pasted the request snippet below and added inline clarifications so your team can drop them into the SSQ cells.

> "Do log exports contain partially reconstructed PII?"
> Our answer: By default, no — logs are sanitized and high-risk fields are redacted or hashed. Logs may contain hashed identifiers for debugging and correlation. Debug exports that include more detail require explicit customer opt-in and RBAC sign-off.

If you want strict no-PII exports we can lock the export pipeline to a customer bucket and apply export_strip_pii_v1.

Let us know a good time for the sync — happy to run through the diagram and the exact cells in the SSQ.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
